summary: This bill requires the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation to implement a "Most Favored Nations Pricing Model" by January 1, 2029, which mandates drug manufacturers to offer their covered drugs to certain Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries at a price no higher than the second-lowest price available in specified developed countries, unless the manufacturer enters into an alternative agreement with the Secretary of Health and Human Services.

scores.thoughts: This bill directly impacts healthcare by mandating a 'most-favored-nation' drug pricing model for Medicare and Medicaid, aiming to lower drug costs. This intervention in drug pricing for public programs leans towards more public control over healthcare costs.

The bill aims to reduce drug costs for individuals covered by Medicare and Medicaid, which are key components of the social safety net. By making prescription drugs more affordable, it effectively expands the benefits and accessibility of these programs.

The bill mandates a CMMI model that ties Medicare and Medicaid drug prices to the second-lowest foreign reference prices, which would reduce federal program expenditures on covered drugs and thereby exert downward pressure on the deficit.

The core purpose of the bill is to require government-directed most-favored-nation drug pricing for Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries, constituting direct federal intervention to lower costs rather than relying on market competition.
